questions.text: उस पादप को पहचानिए जिसमें कृत्रिम संकरण हेतु विपुंसन की आवश्यकता नहीं होती।
questions.text_english: Identify the plant in which emasculation is not required for artificial hybridization.
questions.solution: Papaya (Papaya) is a dioecious plant, meaning male and female flowers are borne on separate plants. Since the flowers are unisexual, there is no need to remove the stamens (emasculation) before artificial hybridization — the female plant naturally lacks stamens. Rice, wheat, and pea are bisexual (hermaphrodite) plants where emasculation is necessary to prevent self-pollination.
questions.solution_hindi: पपीता एक एकलिंगाश्रयी (द्विगृही) पादप है, अर्थात नर और मादा फूल अलग-अलग पौधों पर होते हैं। चूँकि इसके फूल एकलिंगी होते हैं, इसलिए कृत्रिम संकरण से पहले विपुंसन की आवश्यकता नहीं होती। धान, गेहूँ और मटर उभयलिंगी पादप हैं जिनमें विपुंसन अनिवार्य है।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन प्रतिरक्षा तंत्र का संघटक नहीं है?
questions.text_english: Which of the following is not a component of immune system?
questions.solution: Red Blood Cells (RBCs / Erythrocytes) are not a component of the immune system. They function in oxygen transport via haemoglobin. The immune system comprises lymphocytes (B and T cells), plasma proteins (such as antibodies and complement proteins), and bone marrow (which produces immune cells). Hence option C is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: लाल रक्त कोशिकाएँ (एरिथ्रोसाइट) प्रतिरक्षा तंत्र का घटक नहीं हैं; वे हीमोग्लोबिन के माध्यम से ऑक्सीजन परिवहन करती हैं। लसीकाणु, प्लाज़्मा प्रोटीन और अस्थि मज्जा प्रतिरक्षा तंत्र के अभिन्न अंग हैं।

questions.text:
उस विकल्प का चयन कीजिए जो सही कथनों को दर्शाता है:
(i) पीत पिंड (कॉर्पस ल्युटियम) प्रोजेस्टेरोन स्रावित करती है।
(ii) आर्तव चक्र की मध्यावस्था में केवल एफ एस एच (FSH) का स्रवण उच्चतम स्तर पर होता है।
(iii) एल एच सर्ज ग्राफी पुटक को फटने के लिए प्रेरित करता है।
(iv) आर्तव चक्र की स्रावी-प्रावस्था (पीत पिंड प्रावस्था) को प्रचुरोद्भवन-प्रावस्था भी कहते हैं।
questions.text_english:
Select the option that shows correct statements:
(i) Corpus luteum secretes progesterone.
(ii) Only FSH attains a peak level in middle of cycle.
(iii) LH surge induces rupture of graafian follicle.
(iv) Luteal phase of menstrual cycle is also called proliferative phase.
questions.solution: Statement (i) is correct: Corpus luteum, formed after ovulation, secretes progesterone which maintains the uterine lining for implantation. Statement (iii) is correct: the LH surge (sharp rise in LH) triggers the rupture of the Graafian follicle leading to ovulation. Statement (ii) is incorrect because both LH and FSH peak at mid-cycle. Statement (iv) is incorrect because the luteal (secretory) phase is distinct from the proliferative (follicular) phase. Therefore option B is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: कथन (i) सही है: पीत पिंड प्रोजेस्टेरोन स्रावित करती है। कथन (iii) सही है: LH सर्ज ग्राफी पुटक को फटने के लिए प्रेरित करती है। कथन (ii) गलत है क्योंकि मध्यावस्था में LH और FSH दोनों का स्तर उच्चतम होता है। कथन (iv) गलत है क्योंकि स्रावी प्रावस्था और प्रचुरोद्भवन प्रावस्था अलग-अलग हैं।

questions.text:
कुमेलित (बेमेल) युग्म का चयन कीजिए:
(A) विश्व में महा विविध देशों की संख्या – 12
(B) भारत में चावल की आनुवंशिकतः भिन्न प्रभेद (किस्में) – 1000 से कम हैं
(C) वैश्विक जातीय (स्पीशीज)-विविधता के लिए रोबर्ट मेस का आंकलन – संपूर्ण विश्व में 7 मिलियन जातियाँ
(D) प्राणी (जंतु) उद्यान – बाह्य स्थाने संरक्षण
questions.text_english:
Select the mismatched pair:
(A) Mega diversity countries in the world – 12
(B) Genetically different strains of rice in India – Less than 1000
(C) Robert Mays estimation on global species diversity – 7 million species worldwide
(D) Zoological parks – Ex-situ conservation

options.A: विश्व में महा विविध देशों की संख्या – 12
options.B: भारत में चावल की आनुवंशिकतः भिन्न प्रभेद (किस्में) – 1000 से कम हैं
options.C: वैश्विक जातीय (स्पीशीज)-विविधता के लिए रोबर्ट मेस का आंकलन – संपूर्ण विश्व में 7 मिलियन जातियाँ

options_english.A: Mega diversity countries in the world – 12
options_english.B: Genetically different strains of rice in India – Less than 1000
options_english.C: Robert Mays estimation on global species diversity – 7 million species worldwide

questions.solution: Option B is mismatched. India has more than 50,000 genetically different strains of rice (not less than 1000). The correct figure is over 50,000 varieties of rice documented in India, reflecting its enormous agrobiodiversity. All other pairs are correctly matched: there are 12 mega-diversity countries, Robert May estimated 7 million species globally, and zoological parks represent ex-situ conservation.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प B गलत है। भारत में चावल की 1000 से कम नहीं, बल्कि 50,000 से अधिक आनुवंशिक रूप से भिन्न किस्में पाई जाती हैं। शेष सभी युग्म सही हैं।

questions.text: इन पौधों के जीवद्रव्यी संलयन (प्रोटोप्लास्ट युग्मन) द्वारा 'पोमेटो' का निर्माण किया गया:
questions.text_english: Pomato was produced by fusing protoplasts of
questions.solution: Pomato is a somatic hybrid produced by the fusion of protoplasts of Tomato (Solanum lycopersicum) and Potato (Solanum tuberosum). This somatic hybridization technique involves removing the cell walls of both plants using enzymes (cellulase and pectinase) and then fusing the naked protoplasts. The name 'Pomato' is derived from Potato + Tomato.
questions.solution_hindi: पोमेटो एक कायिक संकर (सोमैटिक हाइब्रिड) है जो टमाटर और आलू के प्रोटोप्लास्ट के संलयन द्वारा बनाया गया है। इसका नाम 'पोटेटो + टोमेटो' से आया है।

questions.text: किसी पारितंत्र में विभिन्न प्रजातियाँ विभिन्न स्तरों पर पाई जाती हैं तथा प्रजातियों का ऊर्ध्वाधर वितरण परिलक्षित होता है। इसे कहते हैं –
questions.text_english: In an ecosystem, different species occupy different levels and vertical distribution of species is found. This is called _________.
questions.solution: Stratification refers to the vertical distribution of different species at different levels in an ecosystem, particularly in a forest. For example, in a tropical forest there are distinct layers: the emergent layer (tallest trees), canopy layer, understorey, shrub layer, and ground layer, each occupied by different species. This vertical zonation is called stratification.
questions.solution_hindi: स्तर-विन्यास (Stratification) का अर्थ है पारितंत्र में विभिन्न प्रजातियों का ऊर्ध्वाधर वितरण, जैसे वन में विभिन्न परतें। यही उत्तर सही है।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा 'पवित्र उपवन' मेघालय में पाया जाता है?
questions.text_english: Which of the following sacred groves is found in Meghalaya?
questions.solution: Sacred groves (pवित्र उपवन) are patches of forest protected by local communities due to religious or cultural beliefs. The Jaintia hills (along with Khasi and Garo hills) of Meghalaya are famous for their sacred groves. Bastar and Sarguja are in Chhattisgarh, while Chanda is in Maharashtra. Hence option A is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: मेघालय की जयंतिया पहाड़ियाँ (तथा खासी और गारो पहाड़ियाँ) पवित्र उपवनों के लिए प्रसिद्ध हैं। बस्तर और सरगूजा छत्तीसगढ़ में, और चंदा महाराष्ट्र में हैं।

questions.text: निम्न चित्र में समजात गुणसूत्रों के दो जोड़ों के युग्म बनने के दो तरीकों को दर्शाया गया है। यह किस परिघटना को अभिव्यक्त करता है?
questions.text_english: In the following figure, two ways of pairing of two homologous pairs of chromosomes are shown. Which of the following phenomena is expressed?
questions.solution: The figure shows two equally probable arrangements of two homologous chromosome pairs at Metaphase I of meiosis. In Possibility 1, chromosomes combine as AB and ab; in Possibility 2, they combine as Ab and aB — giving four types of gametes overall. This random, independent orientation of bivalents at the metaphase plate is the chromosomal basis of Mendel's Law of Independent Assortment.
questions.solution_hindi: चित्र में अर्धसूत्री विभाजन की मध्यावस्था-I में दो जोड़े समजात गुणसूत्रों की दो समान संभावित व्यवस्थाएँ दर्शाई गई हैं, जिससे चार प्रकार के युग्मक बनते हैं। यह जीनों के स्वतंत्र संव्यूहन का गुणसूत्रीय आधार है।

questions.text:
कॉलम-I में दी गई मदों का कॉलम-II में दी गई मदों के साथ समुचित मिलान कीजिए तथा सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए:
कॉलम-I: a. बायोलिस्टिक गन, b. काइटिनेज, c. Ti, d. Ca++
कॉलम-II: i. जीवाणु कोशिका, ii. अर्बुद प्रेरण, iii. जंतु कोशिका, iv. कवक कोशिका, v. पादप कोशिका
questions.text_english:
Match Column-I with Column-II and choose the correct option:
Column-I: a. Biolistic gun, b. Chitinase, c. Ti, d. Ca++
Column-II: i. Bacterial cell, ii. Tumour inducing, iii. Animal cell, iv. Fungal cell, v. Plant cell
questions.solution: Biolistic gun (gene gun) is used to introduce DNA into plant cells (v). Chitinase is an enzyme that degrades chitin present in fungal cell walls — used to prepare fungal protoplasts (iv). Ti plasmid of Agrobacterium tumefaciens carries tumour-inducing genes (ii). Ca++ ions are used to make bacterial cell membranes competent to take up foreign DNA (i). Therefore the correct matching is a-v, b-iv, c-ii, d-i, which is option C.
questions.solution_hindi: बायोलिस्टिक गन — पादप कोशिका (v); काइटिनेज — कवक कोशिका (iv); Ti — अर्बुद प्रेरण (ii); Ca++ — जीवाणु कोशिका (i)। अतः सही विकल्प C है।

questions.text: अंगों के उपयोग और अनुपयोग के कारण जीवों के विकास का सुझाव देने (प्रस्तावित करने) वाले वैज्ञानिक का नाम था:
questions.text_english: The idea of use and disuse of organs for evolution of organism was proposed by
questions.solution: Jean-Baptiste Lamarck proposed the Theory of Use and Disuse of Organs in his work 'Philosophie Zoologique' (1809). He stated that organs which are frequently used become stronger and better developed, while organs that are not used gradually become weak and disappear over generations. This is known as Lamarckism. Darwin proposed Natural Selection, Malthus gave population theory, and De Vries proposed Mutation theory.
questions.solution_hindi: लैमार्क ने 'उपयोग एवं अनुपयोग का सिद्धांत' प्रस्तुत किया था। डार्विन ने प्राकृतिक वरण का, माल्थस ने जनसंख्या सिद्धांत का और डी वेरीज़ ने उत्परिवर्तन सिद्धांत का प्रतिपादन किया था।

questions.text: प्लाज़्मिड्स के संबंध में निम्नलिखित कथनों में से कौन सा कथन गलत है?
questions.text_english: Which of the following statements about plasmids is incorrect?

options.A: प्लाज़्मिड्स में जीवाणु कोशिका के अंदर प्रतिकृतियन की क्षमता होती है।
options.B: उनका प्रतिकृतियन क्रोमोसोमी (गुणसूत्रीय) डीएनए द्वारा नियंत्रित होता है।
options.C: वे स्वप्रतिकृतियन करने वाले वृत्ताकार (गोलाकार) बाह्य डीएनए हैं।
options.D: वे अकसर प्रतिजैविक प्रतिरोधी जीनों का संवहन करते हैं।

options_english.A: Plasmids have the ability to replicate within the bacterial cell.
options_english.B: Their replication is controlled by chromosomal DNA.
options_english.C: They are autonomously replicating circular extra-chromosomal DNA.
options_english.D: They often carry antibiotic resistant genes.

questions.solution: Statement B is incorrect. Plasmids replicate autonomously and independently of the bacterial chromosomal DNA — their replication is NOT controlled by chromosomal DNA but by their own origin of replication (ori). Statements A, C, and D are all correct: plasmids do replicate within bacterial cells, they are autonomous circular extra-chromosomal DNA, and they commonly carry antibiotic resistance genes.
questions.solution_hindi: कथन B गलत है। प्लाज़्मिड्स स्वायत्त रूप से प्रतिकृत होते हैं और उनका प्रतिकृतियन गुणसूत्रीय डीएनए द्वारा नियंत्रित नहीं होता।

questions.text: कौन सा संयोजी ऊतक अण्डाशय को श्रोणि भित्ति तथा गर्भाशय के साथ जोड़ता है?
questions.text_english: Which connective tissue connects ovary to pelvic wall and uterus?
questions.solution: Ligaments are bands of fibrous connective tissue that connect bone to bone or hold organs in place. The ovary is held in position by the ovarian ligament (connecting ovary to uterus) and the suspensory ligament (connecting ovary to the pelvic wall). Tendons connect muscles to bones, cartilage cushions joints, and bones form the skeletal framework.
questions.solution_hindi: स्नायु (लिगामेंट) तंतुमय संयोजी ऊतक होता है जो अस्थि को अस्थि से या अंगों को उनकी स्थिति में जोड़ता है। अण्डाशय को गर्भाशय और श्रोणि भित्ति से जोड़ने के लिए लिगामेंट्स होते हैं।

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A): औद्योगिक क्रांति के पश्चात् औद्योगिक क्षेत्रों में गहरे रंग के शलभों की समष्टि में वृद्धि हो गई।
कारण (R): लाइकेन द्वारा आच्छादित वृक्ष औद्योगिक परिवेश में कालिख के कारण काले पड़ गए जिन्होंने गहरे रंग के शलभों को बेहतर छद्मावरण प्रदान किया।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): The population of melanized moths increased in industrial areas after Industrial Revolution.
Reason (R): In Industrial environment lichen covered trees were replaced by soot-covered trees offering better camouflage to dark coloured moths.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) गलत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) गलत है, परन्तु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation for Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation for Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: Both the assertion and reason are true, and the reason correctly explains the assertion. This is the classic example of Industrial Melanism (Biston betularia). Before industrialisation, pale-coloured moths survived better on lichen-covered trees. After industrialisation, soot killed lichens and darkened trees. Dark-coloured moths now blended better with the soot-covered trees and survived (natural selection), while pale moths became easy prey. The dark moth population therefore increased.
questions.solution_hindi: अभिकथन और कारण दोनों सही हैं और कारण, अभिकथन की सही व्याख्या करता है। यह औद्योगिक मेलेनिज्म (बिस्टन बेट्युलेरिया) का उदाहरण है जहाँ काले शलभ कालिख से ढके पेड़ों पर अदृश्य हो जाते थे।

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A): पारजीवी गाय 'रोजी' द्वारा उत्पादित दुग्ध में मानव शिशु हेतु साधारण गाय के दूध की अपेक्षा अधिक संतुलित पोषक तत्व थे।
कारण (R): यह दूध मानव अल्फा-लैक्टाग्लोबुलिन समृद्ध था।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): The milk produced by transgenic cow 'Rosie' was nutritionally more balanced product for human babies than natural cow milk.
Reason (R): It was human protein enriched milk containing human alpha lactaglobulin.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) गलत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) गलत है, परन्तु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation for Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation for Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: Both are true and R correctly explains A. Rosie was the first transgenic cow that produced human protein-enriched milk. The milk contained human alpha-lactalbumin, which is a key whey protein that makes human breast milk nutritionally superior for infants. Because Rosie's milk had this human protein, it was more nutritionally balanced for human babies compared to ordinary cow milk which lacks alpha-lactalbumin.
questions.solution_hindi: दोनों सही हैं और कारण, अभिकथन की व्याख्या करता है। 'रोजी' पारजीवी गाय के दूध में मानव अल्फा-लैक्टाग्लोबुलिन था जो इसे शिशुओं के लिए अधिक पोषक बनाता था।

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A): ऊर्णक कवकीय तंतुओं से जुड़े जीवाणुओं के जाली जैसी संरचना के झुंड हैं जो वाहित मल के द्वितीयक उपचार में पाया जाता है।
कारण (R): ऊर्णक अवायवीय श्वसन द्वारा ठोस अपशिष्टों के पाचन में सहायक हैं।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): Flocs are masses of bacteria associated with fungal filaments in secondary treatment of sewage.
Reason (R): Flocs help in digestion of solid waste by anaerobic respiration.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।

questions.solution: Assertion A is true: flocs are mesh-like structures formed by masses of bacteria associated with fungal filaments, produced during aerobic secondary treatment of sewage in aeration tanks. However, Reason R is false: flocs help in digestion of organic matter by aerobic respiration (not anaerobic). In the secondary treatment aeration tanks, microbes aerobically consume organic wastes. Anaerobic digestion occurs later in sludge digesters. Hence option C is correct.

questions.solution: Assertion A is false: in a terrestrial ecosystem, a much larger fraction of energy actually flows through the Detritus food chain (not the Grazing food chain). Most plant biomass in terrestrial ecosystems dies and enters the detritus pathway rather than being consumed directly by herbivores. Reason R is true: the grazing and detritus food chains are indeed interconnected at various trophic levels. Since A is false and R is true, the correct answer is D.

sub_questions.text_english: Define Humoral immune response.

key_points: Immune response mediated by antibodies present in blood plasma and lymph
Involves B-lymphocytes that differentiate into plasma cells secreting antibodies

sub_questions.solution: Humoral immune response is the type of immunity that is mediated by antibodies circulating in the blood plasma and lymph (body fluids). When an antigen enters the body, B-lymphocytes are activated and differentiate into plasma cells, which secrete specific antibodies. These antibodies bind to and neutralise the antigen.

key_points: IgG (Immunoglobulin G)
IgM (Immunoglobulin M)
IgA, IgE, IgD also acceptable

sub_questions.solution: The two types of antibodies that mediate humoral immune response in humans are IgG (Immunoglobulin G), which is the most abundant antibody in blood and provides long-term immunity, and IgM (Immunoglobulin M), which is the first antibody produced in response to a new infection.

sub_questions.text_english: How does a farmer use dormancy of seed to his advantage?

key_points: Dormant seeds can be stored for longer periods
Prevents premature germination during unfavourable conditions

sub_questions.solution: A farmer uses seed dormancy to his advantage by storing dormant seeds for extended periods without fear of germination. Dormancy prevents seeds from germinating under unfavourable environmental conditions such as drought or extreme temperatures, allowing the farmer to store surplus seeds and use them in subsequent growing seasons.

sub_questions.text_english: Differentiate between pea seed and castor seed.

key_points: Pea seed is non-endospermic (exalbuminous) — food stored in cotyledons
Castor seed is endospermic (albuminous) — food stored in endosperm

sub_questions.solution: Pea seed is non-endospermic (exalbuminous): the endosperm is completely consumed during seed development and food is stored in the fleshy cotyledons. Castor seed is endospermic (albuminous): persistent endosperm is present even in the mature seed, where food is stored in the endosperm tissue.

sub_questions.text_english: Identify the stage of follicle where primary oocyte undergoes first meiotic division. Also mention the products of this division.

key_points: Graafian follicle stage
Products: secondary oocyte (large) and first polar body (small)

sub_questions.solution: The first meiotic division of the primary oocyte occurs at the Graafian follicle stage just before ovulation. This division is an unequal division producing two cells: a large secondary oocyte (which receives most of the cytoplasm) and a small first polar body (which contains very little cytoplasm). The secondary oocyte then proceeds to the second meiotic division, which is completed only if fertilisation occurs.

Study the sequence of bases in a DNA molecule that is shown below and answer the questions.
5' – GAATTC – 3'
3' – CTTAAG – 5'

sub_questions.text: इस प्रकार के अनुक्रम क्या कहलाते हैं? उस एंजाइम का नाम लिखिए जो इस प्रकार के न्युक्लियोटाइड अनुक्रमों की पहचान करता है।
sub_questions.text_english: What are such sequences called? Name the enzyme used that recognises such nucleotide sequences.

key_points: Palindromic sequences
Enzyme: EcoRI (Restriction Endonuclease)

sub_questions.solution: Such sequences are called palindromic sequences. A palindrome in DNA means that the base sequence reads the same on both strands when read in the 5' to 3' direction. The sequence GAATTC is recognised by the restriction enzyme EcoRI (Eco R I), which is a type II restriction endonuclease isolated from Escherichia coli.

sub_questions.text: यह एंजाइम इस किस प्रकार कार्य करते हैं?
sub_questions.text_english: How do these enzymes function?

key_points: They cut DNA at specific palindromic sequences
EcoRI cuts between G and A on both strands, producing sticky ends

sub_questions.solution: Restriction endonucleases inspect the DNA double helix and cut both strands at a specific point within the palindromic recognition sequence. EcoRI cuts between G and A on the 5'-GAATTC-3' sequence of both strands, producing staggered cuts. This generates single-stranded overhanging regions called sticky ends (5' overhangs), which can be joined to complementary sticky ends of other DNA fragments using DNA ligase.

Analyse the following two cases of sex determination in different organisms:
Case I: Males have (XO) sex chromosomes and females have two copies of same sex chromosome (XX).
Case II: Females have two different sex chromosomes (ZW) and males have two copies of same sex chromosome (ZZ).
Identify the type of heterogamety in each case, giving one example of each.

key_points: Case I: Male heterogamety — males produce two types of gametes (X and O); example: Grasshopper
Case II: Female heterogamety — females produce two types of gametes (Z and W); example: Birds (fowl/hen)

sub_questions.solution: In Case I (XO–XX), males are heterogametic because they produce two types of gametes — sperm carrying X chromosome and sperm without sex chromosome (O). This is called male heterogamety. Example: Grasshopper (Locusta). In Case II (ZW–ZZ), females are heterogametic because they produce two types of ova — one carrying Z and one carrying W chromosome. This is called female heterogamety. Example: Birds (e.g., hens/fowl).

sub_questions.text_english: Differentiate between a DNA and RNA nucleotide.

key_points: DNA nucleotide has deoxyribose sugar and Thymine base; RNA nucleotide has ribose sugar and Uracil base

sub_questions.solution: A DNA nucleotide contains deoxyribose sugar (lacks –OH at 2' carbon) and can have one of four bases: Adenine, Guanine, Cytosine, or Thymine. An RNA nucleotide contains ribose sugar (has –OH at 2' carbon) and can have Adenine, Guanine, Cytosine, or Uracil (Thymine is replaced by Uracil in RNA).

Phosphoester bond (between sugar and phosphate group)

sub_questions.solution: Within a single nucleotide, two types of covalent bonds are present: (1) N-glycosidic bond, which links the nitrogenous base to the 1' carbon of the pentose sugar, and (2) Phosphoester bond, which links the phosphate group to the 5' carbon of the pentose sugar.

sub_questions.text_english: Identify the kind of pyramid and with the help of an example explain the conditions where this kind of pyramid is possible in nature.

key_points: Inverted pyramid of biomass
Possible in aquatic ecosystems where phytoplankton (producers) have less biomass than zooplankton

sub_questions.solution: The diagram shows an inverted pyramid of biomass, where the base (Producers — PC) is narrower than the upper level (Primary Consumers — PP). This type of inverted biomass pyramid is found in aquatic ecosystems such as a pond or lake. Here, the phytoplankton (producers) have a very small standing crop biomass but reproduce rapidly, while the zooplankton (primary consumers) accumulate greater biomass due to longer life spans.

sub_questions.text_english: Write any two limitations of ecological pyramids.

key_points: They do not account for the same species occupying different trophic levels
They do not accommodate saprophytes (decomposers)

sub_questions.solution: Two limitations of ecological pyramids are: first, they do not account for the fact that a single species may occupy more than one trophic level simultaneously (e.g., an omnivore eating both plants and animals). Second, they do not give any place to saprophytes (decomposers), which play a crucial role in the ecosystem by breaking down dead organic matter.

sub_questions.text_english: How will biodiversity be affected? (2 points)

key_points: Loss of species diversity — local species may go extinct
Disruption of ecological balance and food web

sub_questions.solution: Loss of biodiversity due to a project in an ecosystem would result in: (1) decline or extinction of local species, reducing overall species richness; and (2) disruption of ecological balance, as food webs and nutrient cycles depend on a variety of species — losing one species can trigger a cascade of effects on others.

sub_questions.text_english: List two major causes of loss of biodiversity.

key_points: Habitat loss and fragmentation
Over-exploitation of species

sub_questions.solution: Two major causes of loss of biodiversity are: (1) Habitat loss and fragmentation — destruction of natural habitats due to deforestation, urbanisation, or development projects is the single greatest driver of biodiversity loss; and (2) Over-exploitation — excessive hunting, poaching, and harvesting of species beyond their reproductive capacity leads to their decline and extinction.

sub_questions.text_english: Do all pollen grains remain viable for the same length of time? Support your answer with two suitable examples.

key_points: No, viability varies greatly between species
Rice/wheat pollen viable for 30 minutes only
Members of Rosaceae/Leguminosae viable for months

sub_questions.solution: No, all pollen grains do not remain viable for the same length of time. Viability varies considerably depending on the species and environmental conditions. For example, pollen grains of rice (Oryza sativa) and wheat (Triticum aestivum) lose viability within 30 minutes of their release. In contrast, pollen grains of members of families Rosaceae (e.g., apple) and Leguminosae (e.g., pea) remain viable for months when stored under appropriate conditions of low humidity and low temperature.

sub_questions.text_english: How are pollen grains stored in pollen banks?

key_points: Stored in liquid nitrogen at -196°C under conditions of low humidity

sub_questions.solution: In pollen banks, pollen grains are stored under conditions of low humidity and low temperature, typically in liquid nitrogen at –196°C. Under these cryogenic conditions, the metabolic activity of pollen is almost completely suspended, allowing them to remain viable for years. Pollen banks are useful for plant breeding programmes.

sub_questions.text_english: What is pedigree analysis? Mention its importance in human genetics. (2 pts.)

key_points: Pedigree is a chart representing inheritance of a trait across generations using standard symbols
Importance: determines inheritance pattern; helps in genetic counselling

sub_questions.solution: Pedigree analysis is the study of the inheritance pattern of a particular trait through several generations of a family, represented in the form of a chart using standard symbols (squares for males, circles for females, shaded symbols for affected individuals). Its importance in human genetics: (1) it helps determine the pattern of inheritance of a trait — whether it is autosomal or sex-linked, dominant or recessive; (2) it is an important tool in genetic counselling to assess the probability of a genetic disorder appearing in future generations of a family.

Other acceptable examples include Phenylketonuria (PKU) and Cystic Fibrosis. In these diseases, an individual must inherit two copies of the defective allele (one from each parent) to show the disease phenotype.

sub_questions.text: हार्डी–वेनबर्ग सिद्धान्त (p² + 2pq + q²) = 1 की व्युत्पति किस प्रकार की गई?
sub_questions.text_english: How is Hardy-Weinberg expression (p² + 2pq + q²) = 1 derived?

key_points: p and q represent allele frequencies of dominant (A) and recessive (a) alleles
p + q = 1 (sum of all allele frequencies = 1)
Expanding (p + q)² gives p² + 2pq + q² = 1 representing genotype frequencies AA, Aa, aa

sub_questions.solution: Let p = frequency of allele A and q = frequency of allele a in a population. Since there are only two alleles, p + q = 1. During random mating, gametes combine randomly. The probability of AA = p × p = p²; probability of Aa = 2 × p × q = 2pq (two ways to form heterozygote); probability of aa = q × q = q². The sum of all genotype frequencies: p² + 2pq + q² = (p + q)² = 1². This binomial expansion gives the Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium equation.

sub_questions.text: ऐसे किन्हीं दो कारकों की सूची बनाइए जो आनुवंशिक संतुलन को विचलित करते हैं।
sub_questions.text_english: List any two factors that disturb the genetic equilibrium.

key_points: Gene flow (migration)
Genetic drift / Natural selection / Mutation / Non-random mating

sub_questions.solution: Two factors that disturb Hardy-Weinberg genetic equilibrium are: (1) Gene flow (migration) — movement of individuals (and hence alleles) between populations changes allele frequencies; and (2) Natural selection — differential survival and reproduction of individuals with certain genotypes alters allele frequencies over generations.

questions.solution: A neat diagram of the megasporangium (ovule) should be drawn showing the following six labelled parts: (1) Funicle — the stalk attaching the ovule to the placenta; (2) Hilum — the junction between funicle and ovule body; (3) Integuments — protective layers surrounding the nucellus (outer and inner); (4) Micropyle — a small opening at one end formed by integuments; (5) Nucellus — the main body of the ovule containing the megaspore mother cell; (6) Chalaza — the basal region of the ovule opposite the micropyle; and the Embryo sac — the female gametophyte inside the nucellus.

sub_questions.text_english: How are morphine and heroin related? Mention the effect each one of them has on human body.

key_points: Heroin is diacetylmorphine — derived by acetylation of morphine
Morphine: strong analgesic, sedative, relieves pain
Heroin: stronger CNS depressant, highly addictive, slows body functions

sub_questions.solution: Morphine and heroin are chemically related: heroin (diacetylmorphine) is synthesised from morphine by acetylation (adding two acetyl groups). Effect of morphine on the human body: it acts as a powerful analgesic (pain reliever) and sedative; it binds to opioid receptors in the brain and CNS, reducing pain perception and producing a sense of well-being. Effect of heroin on the human body: it is a stronger CNS depressant than morphine; it slows down body functions such as heart rate and breathing, causes intense euphoria followed by deep sedation, and is extremely addictive.

sub_questions.text_english: Name the gene in the spores responsible for control of pest.

key_points: cry gene (crystal protein gene / Bt toxin gene)

sub_questions.solution: The gene responsible for pest control present in the spores of Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) is the cry gene (also called the crystal protein gene). This gene encodes Cry proteins, which are insecticidal crystal proteins (delta-endotoxins) that are toxic to specific insect larvae.

sub_questions.text: पीड़क कीटों पर Bt के बीजाणु क्या प्रभाव डालेंगे?
sub_questions.text_english: What effect will the spores of Bt have on insect pest?

key_points: Bt spores produce inactive protoxin; activated in alkaline gut of insects
Active toxin creates pores in midgut epithelium causing cell lysis and insect death

sub_questions.solution: When the spores of Bacillus thuringiensis are ingested by the corn borer larvae, the inactive protoxin (Cry protein) produced by the cry gene is dissolved in the alkaline pH of the insect midgut. The protoxin is then activated by gut proteases and converted into the active toxin form. This active toxin binds to the epithelial cells of the midgut, creates pores in the cell membrane, causing the cells to swell, lyse, and eventually resulting in the death of the insect larva.

sub_questions.text_english: How has corn plants of field B developed resistance against this pest? Explain.

key_points: The cry gene from Bt was introduced into the corn plant genome using genetic engineering
The transgenic corn (Bt corn) expresses the Cry toxin in its tissues, which kills borer larvae when they feed on the plant

sub_questions.solution: The GM corn in field B developed resistance against corn borers through genetic engineering. The cry gene from Bacillus thuringiensis was isolated and inserted into the corn plant genome. As a result, every cell of the Bt corn plant expresses the Cry toxin protein. When corn borer larvae begin to feed on the plant tissue, they ingest the active Cry protein, which damages their gut epithelium and kills them. This intrinsic pest resistance eliminates the need for external pesticide application.

The diagram below shows the distribution of two barnacle species, Chthamalus and Balanus on a rocky sea shore.

When Balanus is experimentally removed, Chthamalus expands its range in lower intertidal zone.

sub_questions.text: इस प्रदर्शन के प्रेक्षणों (साक्ष्यों) के आधार पर इस पारिस्थितिक परिघटना की पहचान कीजिए तथा उसकी परिभाषा भी लिखिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Identify and define the ecological phenomenon demonstrated by this observation.

key_points: Interspecific competition
Competition between Balanus and Chthamalus for space in middle intertidal zone

sub_questions.solution: The ecological phenomenon demonstrated is interspecific competition. Interspecific competition is the interaction between two different species that compete for the same limited resource (in this case, space on the rocky shore). Balanus outcompetes Chthamalus for space in the middle intertidal zone, restricting Chthamalus to the upper intertidal zone. When Balanus is removed, Chthamalus expands into the lower zone, demonstrating that it was held back by competitive exclusion.

sub_questions.text: उस सिद्धान्त की व्याख्या कीजिए जो एक प्रजाति के विलोपन की व्याख्या करता है।
sub_questions.text_english: State the principle that explains the elimination of one species.

key_points: Gause's Competitive Exclusion Principle

sub_questions.solution: The principle that explains the elimination of one species is Gause's Competitive Exclusion Principle. It states that two species competing for the same limited resources cannot coexist indefinitely — the competitively superior species will eventually eliminate (exclude) the inferior one. As seen here, Balanus outcompetes Chthamalus for space in the middle intertidal zone, confining Chthamalus to the upper zone where Balanus cannot survive (due to desiccation).

sub_questions.text: दो विभिन्न जातियाँ एक ही संसाधन के लिए स्पर्धा कर सकती हैं। इसका एक अन्य उदाहरण दीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Two different species can compete for the same resource. Give another example of it.

key_points: Any valid example e.g. Abingdon tortoise and goats competing for food in Galapagos / lions and leopards competing for prey

sub_questions.solution: Another example of two different species competing for the same resource: The Abingdon tortoise (Geochelone elephantopus abingdoni) went extinct within a decade after goats were introduced in its habitat in Galapagos Islands, as goats competed with the tortoises for the same food plants and the goats were competitively superior. Another example is lions and leopards competing for prey animals in the African savannah.

sub_questions.text: प्रकृति में जातियाँ स्पर्धा से कैसे बचाव करती हैं? एक उदाहरण की सहायता से व्याख्या कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: How do species avoid competition in nature? Explain with an example.

key_points: Resource partitioning — species use the same resource differently
Niche differentiation reduces direct competition

sub_questions.solution: Species avoid competition in nature through resource partitioning — by dividing the available resources so that competing species use different parts of the resource in different ways or at different times. This is also called niche differentiation. For example, MacArthur (1958) showed that five species of warblers living in the same tree in North America avoided competition by occupying and foraging in different zones of the tree — top, middle, and lower branches — at different times. By specialising in different microhabitats within the same tree, these species successfully coexisted without intense competition.

sub_questions.text_english: What can you infer about the genotype of parents in crosses I and II?

key_points: Cross I (all tall offspring): TT × tt or TT × TT — parents are TT × tt giving all Tt (tall)
Cross II (3:1 ratio): Tt × Tt — both parents are heterozygous

sub_questions.solution: For Cross I, all 500 offspring are tall and none are dwarf (1:0 ratio). This indicates that one parent is homozygous dominant (TT) and the other is homozygous recessive (tt), giving all Tt (tall) F1 offspring — this is a monohybrid cross between TT and tt. For Cross II, the 375:125 (3:1) tall-to-dwarf ratio indicates that both parents are heterozygous tall (Tt × Tt), which is the F1 self-cross producing the classic Mendelian 3:1 ratio.

sub_questions.text: इन क्रॉसों (संकरण) द्वारा किस आनुवंशिक संकरण का निरूपण हो रहा है?
sub_questions.text_english: Which genetic cross is represented by these crosses?

key_points: Monohybrid cross

sub_questions.solution: These crosses represent a monohybrid cross — a cross involving a single pair of contrasting characters (tall vs. dwarf). Cross I is the P generation cross (TT × tt), Cross II is the F1 self cross (Tt × Tt) giving 3:1 ratio, and Cross III is a test cross (Tt × tt) giving 1:1 ratio.

sub_questions.text: ग्राफ-III के आधार पर किए गए संकरण (क्रॉस) के प्रकार की पहचान कीजिए तथा आनुवंशिकी में इसके महत्त्व का उल्लेख कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Looking at bar graph of cross III, identify the type of cross performed and its importance in genetics.

key_points: Test cross — crossing unknown genotype with homozygous recessive (tt)
Importance: determines whether an organism showing dominant phenotype is homozygous (TT) or heterozygous (Tt)

sub_questions.solution: Cross III, which gives a 250:250 (1:1) tall-to-dwarf ratio, represents a test cross. In a test cross, an individual showing the dominant phenotype (of unknown genotype) is crossed with a homozygous recessive individual (tt). The 1:1 ratio in Cross III confirms that the dominant parent was heterozygous (Tt × tt = 1 Tt : 1 tt). Importance in genetics: a test cross is used to determine the genotype of an organism showing the dominant phenotype — if all offspring are dominant-phenotype, the parent was homozygous (TT); if half are dominant and half recessive, the parent was heterozygous (Tt).

sub_questions.text: क्रॉस I तथा II के दंड ग्राफ से प्राप्त परिणामों के आधार पर आप क्या निष्कर्ष निकाल सकते हैं? प्रदर्शित वंशागति के सिद्धान्त का नाम भी लिखिए।
sub_questions.text_english: What conclusion can you draw from the results of bar graphs of crosses I and II? Name the genetic principle illustrated.

key_points: Tall is dominant over dwarf; F2 shows 3:1 ratio
Mendel's Law of Dominance

sub_questions.solution: From Cross I (all tall) and Cross II (3 tall : 1 dwarf), we can conclude that the tall character is dominant over the dwarf character. In Cross I (F1 generation), all offspring are tall, showing that tallness masks dwarfism. In Cross II (F2 generation), the 3:1 ratio shows that the recessive dwarf trait reappears in one-fourth of the offspring. The genetic principle illustrated is Mendel's Law of Dominance, which states that in a cross between two pure-breeding contrasting characters, only one character (dominant) is expressed in the F1 generation.

sub_questions.text: मानव मादा (स्त्रियों) में निषेचन से प्रारंभ करके कोरकपुटी के अंतरोपण तक की परिघटनाओं का वर्णन कीजिए। उस अवस्थल का भी उल्लेख कीजिए जहाँ निषेचन सम्पन्न होता है।
sub_questions.text_english: Trace the events from fertilization till implantation of blastocyst in human female. Also mention the site where fertilization takes place.

key_points: Fertilization occurs in the ampullary-isthmic junction of fallopian tube
Zygote formation → cleavage → 2-cell, 4-cell, 8-cell, morula stage
Morula moves into uterus, transforms into blastocyst
Blastocyst implants in uterine endometrium around 7th day

sub_questions.solution: Fertilization occurs in the ampullary-isthmic junction of the fallopian tube (oviduct). The acrosome reaction of the sperm releases enzymes that dissolve the zona pellucida, allowing the sperm to fuse with the secondary oocyte. This triggers completion of meiosis II, forming the ovum and second polar body. The male and female pronuclei fuse to form the diploid zygote. The zygote immediately begins mitotic cell divisions (cleavage) while being transported down the fallopian tube towards the uterus. The first cleavage produces a 2-cell stage, followed by 4-cell, 8-cell stages. By the 16-cell stage, a compact ball of cells called the morula is formed, still enclosed in the zona pellucida. As the morula continues dividing, fluid accumulates forming a fluid-filled cavity called the blastocoel, transforming it into the blastocyst. The blastocyst consists of an outer layer of cells (trophoblast) and an inner cell mass (embryoblast). The zona pellucida dissolves and the blastocyst attaches to the endometrium of the uterus around the 7th day after fertilisation — this process is called implantation. The trophoblast cells penetrate the endometrial lining, embedding the blastocyst into the uterine wall to establish pregnancy.

sub_questions.text: केस-I – स्त्री – परीक्षण रिपोर्ट सामान्य। पुरुष – शुक्राणु सामान्य हैं, परन्तु अधिवृषण (ऐपिडिडिमस) तथा शुक्रवाहक (वास डेफेरेंस) आपस में जुड़े नहीं हैं।
sub_questions.text_english: Case I – Female – Normal Reports. Male – Normal sperms but no connection between epididymis and vas deferens.

key_points: ICSI (Intracytoplasmic Sperm Injection) — sperm retrieved directly from epididymis and injected into egg

sub_questions.solution: For Case I, the recommended Assisted Reproductive Technology is ICSI (Intracytoplasmic Sperm Injection). Since the male has normal sperms but the epididymis and vas deferens are not connected, sperm cannot be ejaculated normally. In ICSI, sperm are retrieved directly from the epididymis by surgical aspiration (PESA — Percutaneous Epididymal Sperm Aspiration) and a single sperm is directly injected into the cytoplasm of the retrieved egg in the laboratory, after which the fertilised embryo is transferred to the uterus.

sub_questions.text: केस-II – स्त्री – अंड सामान्य हैं परन्तु अंडवाहिनी अवरोधित है। पुरुष – शुक्राणु सामान्य हैं। पुरुष की परीक्षण रिपोर्ट सामान्य है।
sub_questions.text_english: Case II – Female – Normal eggs but Fallopian tube blocked. Male – Normal sperms. Male reports are normal.

key_points: IVF-ET (In Vitro Fertilisation followed by Embryo Transfer) — ZIFT

sub_questions.solution: For Case II, the recommended ART is IVF-ET (In Vitro Fertilisation – Embryo Transfer), also known as the test tube baby technique. Since the fallopian tube is blocked, natural fertilisation cannot occur. Eggs are retrieved from the woman's ovaries by laparoscopy and fertilised with the partner's sperm in the laboratory. The resulting embryo (at 8-cell stage) is transferred into the fallopian tube as ZIFT (Zygote Intra Fallopian Transfer) or into the uterus as IUT (Intra Uterine Transfer) to complete development.

sub_questions.text: केस-III – स्त्री – सामान्य रिपोर्ट। पुरुष – वीर्य में शुक्राणुओं की संख्या बहुत कम तथा कम गतिशील।
sub_questions.text_english: Case III – Female – Normal Reports. Male – Low sperm count with less motility.

key_points: ICSI (Intracytoplasmic Sperm Injection) — single sperm injected directly into egg

sub_questions.solution: For Case III, the recommended ART is ICSI (Intracytoplasmic Sperm Injection). Since the male has very low sperm count (oligospermia) and reduced sperm motility, natural fertilisation or even IVF may not be feasible. In ICSI, a single healthy sperm is selected and directly injected into the cytoplasm of a retrieved egg using a micro-needle. The fertilised embryo is then cultured and transferred to the uterus.

sub_questions.text: ताँबा मोचक अंतः गर्भाशयी युक्तियाँ (आई यू डी) अत्यंत प्रभावशाली तथा लोकप्रिय गर्भनिरोधक युक्तियाँ हैं। किन्हीं दो ताँबा मोचक आई यू डी के नाम लिखिए। ऐसे दो कारण लिखिए जो इन्हें प्रभावी गर्भनिरोधक बनाते हैं।
sub_questions.text_english: Copper releasing intrauterine devices are very effective and popular contraceptive devices. Name any two copper releasing IUDs. Write two reasons that make them effective contraceptives.

key_points: CuT (Copper-T) and Cu7 (Copper-7)
Copper ions suppress sperm motility; create hostile uterine environment preventing implantation

sub_questions.solution: Two copper-releasing IUDs are: CuT (Copper-T) and Cu7 (Copper-7). Two reasons that make copper IUDs effective contraceptives: (1) Copper ions released from the device are toxic to sperm — they suppress sperm motility and fertilising capacity, thus preventing fertilisation; (2) The IUD creates changes in the uterine environment that make it hostile to implantation — it increases phagocytosis of sperm and alters the endometrial lining, preventing the blastocyst from implanting even if fertilisation occurs.

sub_questions.text: वाटसन तथा क्रीक द्वारा प्रस्तुत डीएनए की द्विकुंडली संरचना किन दो खोजों पर आधारित थी? उन दो वैज्ञानिकों के नामों का उल्लेख कीजिए, जिन्होंने यह खोज की थी।
sub_questions.text_english: Watson and Crick's discovery of double helical structure was based on which two findings. Also mention the name of the scientists associated with these findings.

key_points: X-ray diffraction data of DNA by Rosalind Franklin and Maurice Wilkins
Chargaff's rules — A=T and G=C (base pairing ratios)

sub_questions.solution: Watson and Crick's double helical model of DNA (1953) was based on two key findings: (1) X-ray diffraction data of DNA produced by Rosalind Franklin and Maurice Wilkins, which revealed that DNA is a helix with a uniform diameter of about 2 nm, and that the bases are stacked 0.34 nm apart; (2) Chargaff's Rules (proposed by Erwin Chargaff), which stated that in any DNA molecule, the amount of Adenine always equals Thymine (A = T) and the amount of Guanine always equals Cytosine (G = C), suggesting complementary base pairing.

sub_questions.text: डीएनए की द्विकुंडलीय संरचना की कोई तीन प्रमुख विशेषताओं को लिखिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Write down the salient features of double helix structure of DNA (any three points).

key_points: Two antiparallel polynucleotide chains coiled around a common axis
Bases are inside; sugar-phosphate backbone is outside
Complementary base pairing: A-T (2 H-bonds) and G-C (3 H-bonds); pitch of helix is 3.4 nm with 10 base pairs per turn

sub_questions.solution: Three salient features of the double helix structure of DNA are: (1) it is made of two polynucleotide chains that are antiparallel to each other — one chain runs 5'→3' and the other runs 3'→5'; they coil around a common helical axis in a right-handed manner; (2) the backbone of each strand consists of alternating deoxyribose sugar and phosphate groups on the outside, while the nitrogenous bases are on the inside, stacked perpendicular to the helix axis; (3) the two strands are held together by complementary base pairing through hydrogen bonds — Adenine pairs with Thymine by 2 hydrogen bonds (A=T) and Guanine pairs with Cytosine by 3 hydrogen bonds (G≡C). The helix has a pitch of 3.4 nm with approximately 10 base pairs per turn.

इसके संगत टेम्पलेट रज्जु तथा अनुलेखित होने वाले mRNA रज्जु का आरेख ध्रुवणता दर्शाते हुए बनाइए।
दिया गया कोडिंग स्ट्रैंड: 5' - ATG ACC GTA TTT TCT GTA GTG CCC GTA CTT CAG GCA TAA 3'
sub_questions.text_english:
Write the corresponding template strand and m-RNA strand that will be transcribed along with its polarity.
Given coding strand: 5' - ATG ACC GTA TTT TCT GTA GTG CCC GTA CTT CAG GCA TTA 3'

key_points: Template strand: 3' - TAC TGG CAT AAA AGA CAT CAC GGG CAT GAA GTC CGT ATT - 5'
mRNA: 5' - AUG ACC GUA UUU UCU GUA GUG CCC GUA CUU CAG GCA UAA - 3'

sub_questions.solution:
Given coding strand: 5'- ATG ACC GTA TTT TCT GTA GTG CCC GTA CTT CAG GCA TAA -3'

Corresponding template strand (antiparallel and complementary to coding strand):
3'- TAC TGG CAT AAA AGA CAT CAC GGG CAT GAA GTC CGT ATT -5'

Transcribed mRNA strand (same sequence as coding strand but with U replacing T, read 5'→3'):
5'- AUG ACC GUA UUU UCU GUA GUG CCC GUA CUU CAG GCA UAA -3'

The mRNA has 5' polarity at the start (AUG = start codon) and ends with UAA (stop codon).

sub_questions.text: यदि अनुलेखित mRNA का GUA एक इंट्रॉन है तो mRNA के बनने/परिपक्व परिष्कृत hnRNA रज्जु में शामिल अनुक्रम को दर्शाइए: (1) एक जीवाणु में
sub_questions.text_english: If GUA of transcribed mRNA is an intron, then depict the sequence involved in formation of mRNA / mature / processed hnRNA strand: (1) In a bacterium

key_points: In a bacterium, introns are absent — no splicing occurs; mRNA sequence remains unchanged as bacteria have no introns

sub_questions.solution: In a bacterium, introns do not exist — prokaryotic genes are continuous (no introns). Therefore, no splicing occurs. The entire mRNA sequence including the GUA codon would be present in the mRNA as transcribed: 5'-AUG ACC GUA UUU UCU GUA GUG CCC GUA CUU CAG GCA UAA-3'. The mRNA in a bacterium is the same as the primary transcript.

sub_questions.text: (2) एक मानव में
sub_questions.text_english: (2) In humans

key_points: In humans, GUA intron is spliced out; mature mRNA lacks GUA sequence
Mature mRNA: AUG ACC UUU UCU GUA GUG CCC GUA CUU CAG GCA UAA (GUA removed)

sub_questions.solution: In humans (eukaryotes), the primary transcript is first formed as hnRNA (heterogeneous nuclear RNA). Since GUA is an intron, it is removed by splicing (via snRNP spliceosome complex). The mature processed mRNA after removal of the GUA intron would be: 5'-AUG ACC UUU UCU GUA GUG CCC GUA CUU CAG GCA UAA-3'. Additionally, in humans, the mature mRNA receives a 5' methyl-guanosine cap and a 3' poly-A tail before being exported from the nucleus for translation.

sub_questions.text: मनुष्य में स्थानांतरण (रूपांतरण) प्रक्रम के पश्चात् बनने वाली पॉलिपेप्टाइड शृंखला में अमीनो अम्लों की संख्या कितनी होगी?
sub_questions.text_english: How many amino acids the resulting polypeptide will have after the process of translation in humans?

key_points: After removal of GUA intron, count codons from AUG to stop codon UAA excluding stop codon

sub_questions.solution: After splicing out the GUA intron in humans, the mature mRNA is: 5'-AUG ACC UUU UCU GUA GUG CCC GUA CUU CAG GCA UAA-3'. Counting codons: AUG-ACC-UUU-UCU-GUA-GUG-CCC-GUA-CUU-CAG-GCA-UAA. That is 12 codons total, of which UAA is the stop codon and does not code for an amino acid. The AUG (start codon) codes for methionine. Therefore the polypeptide will have 11 amino acids.

sub_questions.text: उस रोग कारक प्रोटोजोआ प्रजाति का नाम लिखिए जो अत्यंत गंभीर और घातक मलेरिया नामक रोग के लिए उत्तरदायी है।
sub_questions.text_english: Name the protozoan species that is responsible for causing the most serious and even fatal malarial disease.

key_points: Plasmodium falciparum

sub_questions.solution: Plasmodium falciparum is the protozoan species responsible for the most serious and potentially fatal form of malaria called malignant or falciparum malaria (also known as cerebral malaria). Unlike P. vivax and P. malariae, P. falciparum can infect all stages of red blood cells and can block capillaries in the brain.

sub_questions.text: उस परपोषी का नाम लिखिए जिसमें यह रोगजनक प्रोटोजोआ अपनी लैंगिक अवस्थाएँ पूर्ण करता है। होने वाले परिवर्तनों की व्याख्या कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Name the host in which the parasite completes its sexual stages and explain the changes taking place.

key_points: Sexual cycle (sporogony) occurs in female Anopheles mosquito
Gametocytes from human blood develop into gametes in mosquito gut, fertilisation forms ookinete, then oocyst, then sporozoites which migrate to salivary glands

sub_questions.solution: The parasite completes its sexual stages in the female Anopheles mosquito (the definitive host). When a female Anopheles mosquito bites an infected human, it ingests gametocytes (male and female) along with the blood meal. Inside the mosquito's stomach, the gametocytes differentiate into gametes and fertilisation occurs, forming a zygote called the ookinete. The ookinete penetrates the stomach wall and develops into an oocyst on the outer surface. Within the oocyst, repeated mitotic divisions produce thousands of sporozoites. The oocyst then ruptures and sporozoites are released, which migrate to the salivary glands of the mosquito. When this infected mosquito bites a healthy person, sporozoites are injected into the human bloodstream along with saliva.

sub_questions.text: रुधिर (रक्त) प्रवाह में प्रविष्ट होने के पश्चात् यह परजीवी मानव शरीर को किस प्रकार क्षति पहुँचाता है?
sub_questions.text_english: How does the parasite damage the human body after entering the blood stream?

key_points: Sporozoites enter liver, multiply as merozoites
Merozoites infect RBCs, feed on haemoglobin, lyse RBCs releasing toxins causing chills and fever

sub_questions.solution: After entering the bloodstream, the sporozoites travel to the liver cells (hepatocytes) where they undergo asexual multiplication (exo-erythrocytic schizogony), producing thousands of merozoites. The merozoites are then released into the blood and invade red blood cells (RBCs). Inside the RBCs, they feed on haemoglobin and multiply further through erythrocytic schizogony. The RBCs rupture periodically, releasing more merozoites along with metabolic waste products (haemozoin/malaria pigment) and toxins into the blood. This rupture of RBCs causes the recurring cycles of chills, high fever, and sweating. Repeated destruction of RBCs leads to anaemia, organ dysfunction, and in P. falciparum infections, blockage of cerebral capillaries (cerebral malaria), which can be fatal.

sub_questions.text: इस रोग के नियंत्रण हेतु स्थानिक महामारी क्षेत्र में इसकी रोकथाम के दो प्रभावशाली तरीकों (उपायों) का सुझाव दीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Suggest two effective preventive measures to control the spread of this disease in endemic regions.

key_points: Elimination of mosquito breeding sites (draining stagnant water)
Use of mosquito nets, repellents, and insecticides like DDT

sub_questions.solution: Two effective preventive measures to control malaria in endemic regions are: (1) Mosquito control — eliminating breeding sites of Anopheles mosquitoes by draining stagnant water (ponds, puddles, containers), using larvicides like Bacillus thuringiensis israelensis (Bti), and spraying insecticides such as DDT or pyrethrum in houses; (2) Personal protection — using insecticide-treated bed nets (ITNs), applying mosquito repellents, wearing protective full-sleeved clothing especially at dusk and dawn when Anopheles mosquitoes are most active.

sub_questions.text: जैव-उर्वरक क्या हैं?
sub_questions.text_english: What are bio-fertilizers?

key_points: Organisms that enrich the nutrient quality of the soil; used as alternatives to chemical fertilisers

sub_questions.solution: Bio-fertilizers are organisms (mainly microorganisms) that enrich the nutrient quality of the soil when applied to seeds, plant surfaces, or soil. They help in fixing atmospheric nitrogen, solubilising insoluble phosphates, or producing plant growth-promoting substances, thereby increasing soil fertility naturally without the harmful effects of chemical fertilisers.

sub_questions.text: जैविक खेती में जैव-उर्वरक के रूप में उपयोग किए जाने वाले विभिन्न प्रकार के सूक्ष्म-जीवों के नाम लिखिए तथा व्याख्या कीजिए कि यह मृदा की उर्वरता बढ़ाने में किस प्रकार योगदान करते हैं।
sub_questions.text_english: Name the different types of microorganisms used as bio-fertilizers in organic farming and explain how each contributes to soil fertility.

key_points: Bacteria: Rhizobium (symbiotic N-fixation in legume root nodules), Azospirillum/Azotobacter (free-living N-fixation)
Cyanobacteria/Blue-green algae: Anabaena, Nostoc — fix atmospheric nitrogen in paddy fields
Fungi: Mycorrhizae — increase phosphate absorption and water uptake by plants

sub_questions.solution: The different types of microorganisms used as bio-fertilizers in organic farming are: (1) Bacteria — Rhizobium forms symbiotic associations with leguminous plant roots, living in root nodules and fixing atmospheric nitrogen into ammonia which is directly available to the plant. Free-living bacteria like Azotobacter and Azospirillum fix atmospheric nitrogen in the soil. (2) Cyanobacteria (Blue-green algae) — Anabaena, Nostoc, and Oscillatoria are important bio-fertilizers in paddy fields. They fix atmospheric nitrogen and also add organic matter to the soil, improving soil structure and fertility. (3) Fungi (Mycorrhizae) — Glomus and other mycorrhizal fungi form symbiotic associations with plant roots. The fungal hyphae greatly increase the surface area for water and mineral absorption, especially phosphate. They also enhance plant tolerance to drought and soil pathogens.

sub_questions.text: रासायनिक उर्वरकों की अपेक्षा जैव-उर्वरकों के उपयोग के दो लाभ लिखिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Write two advantages of using bio-fertilizers over chemical fertilizers.

key_points: Eco-friendly and do not cause soil/water pollution
Improve long-term soil health and structure

sub_questions.solution: Two advantages of using bio-fertilizers over chemical fertilizers are: (1) they are eco-friendly and do not cause soil degradation or water pollution — unlike chemical fertilizers which can cause eutrophication of water bodies and destroy soil microbiota; (2) they improve long-term soil health by increasing microbial activity, organic matter content, and soil structure, whereas chemical fertilizers lead to soil acidification and deterioration of soil quality over time.
